- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are volatile, model underestimates; adjust upward by 5–15% if recent price action shows upward momentum.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >50% above recent mean), reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 3–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often lags; add 5–10% to forecast starting from day of sentiment turn.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day mean, apply downward correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits short-term noise; use 20–30% smoothing filter on forecast values.
